$comment: Machine-readable index of the mcp-broker samples. Written for an agent scanning the repo: everything needed to choose a sample and run it is here, without opening the folders. Paths are relative to this file's directory.

setup.why: Links this repo's broker and provider packages into samples/node_modules so every sample resolves them by their real published names. Fast and offline: the dependencies are file: links, nothing is fetched.
setup.requires: Node >= 20.11.0. Node 22 is what the samples are verified on; Node 20 has no global WebSocket, so any sample that opens a provider socket from Node needs --experimental-websocket or a ws polyfill assigned to globalThis.WebSocket.

rules.$comment: The invariants every sample obeys, and every failure in the field so far came from breaking one of these.
rules.transportPathPairing: The provider URL and the transport class are one decision. /provider/<slot> carries plain JSON-RPC frames and pairs with DirectTransport. /providers carries {provider, payload} envelopes and pairs with MultiplexTransport. /providers/<slot> is NEITHER: it is accepted as a raw-WebSocket CLIENT of a slot with that literal name, and nothing ever answers.
rules.handlersBeforeConnect: Assign onMessage (or hand the transport to an MCP server) BEFORE calling connect(). The broker runs initialize against a newly aggregated provider immediately and drops it from _all silently if the handshake times out.
rules.releaseTheSlot: Call transport.close() when the provider goes away. In a browser that means window.addEventListener('pagehide', ...). Without it a reload is refused by its own predecessor with WebSocket close code 1008.
rules.originCheckAppliesToServedPages: A page served by the broker's own www mount is still a browser origin. /<slot>/mcp, /<slot>/sse and /<slot>/messages compare the Origin header against allowedOrigins verbatim; with no list configured, no browser origin passes. A request with no Origin header (Node, MCP Inspector, any server-side SDK) always passes.
rules.stdioBridgeTargetsAll: MCP_BROKER_STDIO_PROVIDER must name _all, not a real slot. The bridge gates every frame including initialize on the slot being occupied, so a host that starts before the provider fails permanently. _all exists from startup, answers initialize itself, and pushes tools/list_changed as providers join.
rules.neverRebuildAggregatedToolNames: Through _all a tool is named <slot>-<tool>, but the broker caps long names, hashes the overflow and appends -2 to break ties. Read the name from tools/list; never build it by concatenation.
rules.aggregateIsOptIn: A WebSocket provider or a stdioUpstreams entry joins _all only when it asks (transport option { aggregate: true }, or "aggregate": true in the config). mcpServers (remote upstreams) and mcpbBundles join by default and opt out with "aggregate": false.

reservedSlots._broker: Introspection and self-documentation. Always present, needs no provider. Tools: broker_info, providers_list, provider_status, broker_guide (integration docs as Markdown), broker_diagnose (live problem report with symptom, evidence and fix).
reservedSlots._all: Live aggregate of every opted-in provider. Present from startup, answers initialize itself, prefixes tool names with <slot>-, pushes notifications/tools/list_changed as providers come and go. The right target for an MCP host.

samples.title: Publish an MCP server from a browser page
samples.useThisWhen: A tool must run in a browser (DOM, canvas, WebGPU, a user session) and be callable by an MCP client.
samples.run: cd samples && npm install && npm run browser-provider
samples.expect: A browser opens at http://localhost:3000/. Press Publish, then the initialize + tools/list + tools/call button; the page log ends with 'round trip complete'. The headless client prints 'round trip complete: Node -> broker -> browser page -> broker -> Node.'

files.role: THE INTEGRATION. Four blocks marked WRONG CHOICE, each naming the wrong line and the failure it produces.
Page shell; holds the import map that stands in for a bundler.
A hand-written MCP server that knows nothing about the broker.
Starts the broker with the four env vars this topology needs and prints the equivalent shell command.
Copies the provider SDK's ESM build into public/vendor/.

samples.title: Wire the broker into an MCP host's config file
samples.useThisWhen: Configuring Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code to see the broker's slots.
samples.run: cd samples && npm install && node host-config/check.mjs
samples.expect: Six numbered steps ending in 'BOTH ENTRIES WORK AGAINST ONE PROCESS.' Step 2 completes initialize with no provider connected; step 5 shows tools/list_changed arriving when a provider joins late.

files.role: The two-entry pattern, with the reasoning in a _readme array. Copy the mcpServers block.
Same with client OAuth and provider authentication, and the difference between them spelled out.
The broker config entry 1 points at. Runnable.
Authorization template. NOT runnable: references certs and an authorization server that do not exist here.
Drives both entries exactly as a host would, over stdio and over HTTP, against one process.

samples.keyPoint: Entry 1 spawns the broker and bridges it over stdio, pinned to _all. Entry 2 is a URL to the listener entry 1 already opened, and must NEVER be a second command entry: that starts a second broker, which either dies with EADDRINUSE or comes up sharing no slots with the first and silently missing every tool.

samples.title: Connect, refuse, release, restart, reconnect: the life of a provider socket
samples.useThisWhen: A slot is stuck, you saw close code 1008, or you are choosing between DirectTransport and MultiplexTransport.
samples.run: cd samples && npm install && node provider-lifecycle/run.mjs
samples.expect: Six narrated steps, about 30 seconds, with the broker's own log interleaved. Step 3 reproduces the 1008 refusal on purpose and prints the broker's full reason string. Step 5 kills and restarts the broker and shows that MultiplexTransport retries while DirectTransport does not.

files.role: The scenario. Both providers built inline so every callback is visible.
Starts and SIGKILLs a broker process, so the restart is a crash rather than a polite shutdown.

keyPoints: onOpen fires BEFORE the 1008 refusal: the WebSocket handshake succeeds and the refusal is a close frame that follows. Never treat onOpen as proof you own the slot.
The NEWCOMER is refused and the incumbent is untouched, so the page you are looking at is the one that breaks while the page that is gone keeps the slot.
DirectTransport never reconnects. MultiplexTransport does, with backoff, and re-announces its slots.

Under Node the automatic retry stops after the first attempt that lands while the broker is down, because Node's built-in WebSocket fires error but never close for a connection that failed to open. Browsers fire close(1006) and the loop keeps going. The sample says so and recovers by hand.

settings.MCP_BROKER_PROVIDER_HEARTBEAT_MS: 30000 default, 0 disables. Reaps a socket that stopped answering pings.
settings.MCP_BROKER_PROVIDER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS: 60000 default, 0 disables. Deadline for one provider answer.
settings.MCP_BROKER_PROVIDER_TAKEOVER: reject | liveness | always, default liveness. 'always' is honoured only when provider authentication is configured.

samples.title: The broker as your application's HTTP host
samples.useThisWhen: Shipping a web app whose live state should be callable over MCP, and you want one process, one origin and no start-order dependency.
samples.run: cd samples && npm install && node app-host/run.mjs
samples.expect: The banner lists TWO static mounts and the browser opens at http://localhost:3400/app/, not at /. The page publishes itself on load with no button. client.mjs increments a counter five times and the number on the page changes while you watch.

files.role: THE SAMPLE. Two www.mounts entries, www.open on a sub-path, the origin list, the liveness defaults written out.
The application, which is also the provider. Publishes on load.
Mounted at /, a different directory from the app.
Sets exactly one env var, MCP_BROKER_CONFIG, and lets the file carry the rest.
Drives the open page over Streamable HTTP.

keyPoints: MCP_BROKER_WWW_DIR mounts exactly one directory at /. There is no env var for an arbitrary set of mounts; www.mounts in the config file is the only way.
Paths inside a config file resolve against the config file's directory; env-var paths resolve against the working directory.

www.open accepts true, an absolute path, or an absolute URL on this broker's own origin. A foreign origin is refused. Keep the trailing slash on a sub-path, or the page's relative script URLs resolve one level too high.

samples.title: Embed the broker as a library with WsTunnelBuilder
samples.useThisWhen: Your application is already a Node process and should BE the broker rather than spawn one.
samples.run: cd samples && npm install && node embedded/server.mjs --once
samples.expect: The broker starts in-process, an in-process provider is registered on 'job-runner' with no socket, it is called through openInternalClient and then over HTTP, and getProvidersInfo() lists four slots. Ends with 'stopped cleanly'.

files.role: The whole sample: builder, loopback transport, internal client, shutdown.

keyPoints: await start() and catch it: it rejects on a listen failure and the rejection carries the whole diagnosis, including err.cause with the original errno.
await stop(): it closes sockets, clears the heartbeat and request-timeout timers and closes the listener.
In a loopback transport both halves face the BROKER: the broker calls send() with a client's request, and you call onMessage() with your server's answer. The broker assigns onMessage and onClose.

A loopback provider CANNOT join _all: registerLoopbackProvider takes no aggregate argument and the aggregate server is not public. To reach _all, publish over a DirectTransport to your own 127.0.0.1 address with { aggregate: true }.

sharedLibrary.role: A minimal MCP client over Streamable HTTP in ~90 lines of fetch. Isomorphic: the same file runs in Node and, copied into a page's vendor directory, in a browser.
publishProvider({ brokerUrl, slot, aggregate, tools, call }): a provider in Node in one call, obeying the same three rules as the browser sample.
Resolves the broker's CLI inside node_modules and spawns it with a given environment.
Copies the provider package's ESM build into a directory the broker serves, so a page can import it with no bundler.

diagnosis.$comment: Before reading any of these samples, ask the broker itself.
diagnosis.guide: Call the broker_guide tool on the _broker slot, or read broker://guide/index, broker://guide/publish-provider, broker://guide/connect-client, broker://guide/host-config, broker://guide/deploy, broker://guide/troubleshooting.
diagnosis.diagnose: Call the broker_diagnose tool on the _broker slot. It returns live per-slot state plus proven problems, each with a symptom, the evidence behind it and a fix.
diagnosis.howToReachIt: POST an initialize frame to http://<broker>/_broker/mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, then reuse the Mcp-Session-Id it returns. samples/lib/mcp-http-client.mjs does exactly that, and samples/app-host/client.mjs --diagnose is a one-line example.
